qc.label_under_test: A second, mirrored labelling clause that casts the speaker or the listener: after one clause casts someone as something (sees him as a hero, calls her a liar), a following clause casts me, us or you (and she sees me as a nuisance, they treat us as outsiders, and he calls you a snob); it fires on the 'as' or 'a' right after 'me'/'us'/'you'. 'You' fires when you did the first labelling (you treat them as family, and they treat you as staff); after 'I see him as...', a second clause casting you stays weak. The same second clause aimed at him, her or them is weak, as is a one-way label of me or you with no earlier labelling clause, or me labelled in the first clause and answering back. Strongest when a sentence of setting comes first.

fire: The office party dragged on past midnight. My boss sees the new intern as a genius, and she sees me as a nuisance.
We moved to the village last spring. The locals treat the old baker as family, but they treat us as outsiders.
The reunion was awkward from the start. Everyone called Mark a legend, and then they called me a has-been.
It was a long winter in the cabin. Grandma saw my cousin as a saint and saw me as a troublemaker.
The tour bus finally reached the hotel. The manager treated the band as royalty, while the staff treated us as luggage.
Rain hammered the windows all afternoon. You treat them as family, and they treat you as staff.
The debate club met every Thursday. You call him a bully, and he calls you a snob.
The new semester began with a heavy fog. The teacher regards Lena as a star pupil and regards me as a lost cause.
